name: King of Geder
overview: The King of Geder was a male ruler identified as one of the thirty-one kings defeated by Joshua during the Israelite conquest of Canaan. While his tribal affiliation and other personal details are not recorded, his defeat is noted in the biblical account, highlighting his role as an adversary to Israel during this period.
namesAndTitles: The title 'King of Geder' simply denotes his position as the monarch over the city or region of Geder. This designation is straightforward and does not carry a special theological meaning beyond identifying his rule, as noted in Joshua 12:13.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships or personal connections for the King of Geder beyond his identification as one of the kings defeated by Joshua.
scriptureSignificance: The King of Geder's significance lies in his inclusion among the defeated kings listed in Joshua 12:13, marking the fulfillment of God's promise to give Israel the land of Canaan through Joshua's leadership. His defeat symbolizes the divine judgment against the Canaanite nations and the establishment of Israel's possession of the Promised Land, underscoring God's faithfulness to His covenant people.
